summary: Batched request retry coordinator normalizes per-call idempotency metadata, causing tool invocation order swaps and duplicate side-effects
description: Customer reports that when sending a single batched generate request containing multiple tool/function calls (tool-A then tool-B), a mid-request retry triggered by the retry coordinator results in tool-B executing before tool-A on downstream systems and occasionally double-executing one tool. The customer is using the Go SDK with per-tool idempotency tokens set on each function/tool invocation. The symptoms started after a coordinator change that coalesces and requeues partial batches for retry.
impact: Customer-facing job pipeline at Acme DataWorks is producing out-of-order downstream side effects (database writes and webhook calls). Some jobs are duplicated or applied in the wrong order, causing data integrity issues for a small percentage (~0.7%) of runs. Customer is on Dedicated tier and has many parallel long-running sessions; they requested a hotfix or workaround because this affects production data.
logs:
Customer provided excerpt from their webhook consumer showing order swap:
- 2026-03-09T21:14:53.102Z POST /webhook -> payload.webhookId=web-456 processed -> created row id 987
- 2026-03-09T21:14:53.198Z POST /webhook -> payload.eventId=evt-123 processed -> created row id 988

Orchestrator logs (trim):
- 2026-03-09T21:14:52.950Z batch-req-51 ACCEPTED
- 2026-03-09T21:14:53.000Z serving-runtime: partial-failure stream-reset
- 2026-03-09T21:14:53.010Z coordinator: requeue-partial-batch batch-req-51 shard=3
- 2026-03-09T21:14:53.012Z coordinator: normalized-metadata idempotency-scope=REQUEST (was PER_TOOL)
- 2026-03-09T21:14:53.050Z worker-7: re-dispatched tools [sendWebhook, recordEvent]
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: coordinator's requeue path rewrites idempotency baggage to a request-level scope for dedup detection, losing the per-tool tokens that guarantee ordering semantics. The requeue implementation also reorders the tool list when reconstructing partial batches (uses a hash-based placement across shards). Reproduction in staging with iptables injection reproduces the ordering swap and duplicate execution when per-tool idempotency tokens are dropped.

What we checked:
- SDK: confirmed customer sends per-tool token headers correctly (Go SDK 1.8.2).
- Orchestrator: recent deploy 2026-03-02 introduced batching coalescer change (PR #4287).
- Serving-runtime: logs show ACKs for both tool calls but timestamps show reordered dispatch after coordinator requeue.
- Downstream dedup: customer uses idempotency tokens to dedupe writes; when tokens were normalized to request-level, dedupe failed to be per-tool and allowed duplicates.

Current risk: high for pipelined workflows with side-effects. We can reproduce locally and in a dedicated staging cluster.
comments: Support (Maya): Collected customer logs and minimal repro. Escalating to runtime/orchestrator. URL to session logs: https://console.redwood/team/support/sessions/abc123

SRE (Liam): Reproduced in staging with packet-drop approach. Confirmed coordinator normalized idempotency on requeue. Tentative root cause: coordinator code path that merges 'baggage' for partial batches uses 'mergeMetadata' which falls back to REQUEST scope when per-item metadata differs across shard replicas.

Eng (Priya Nair): PR 4287 added batch coalescer optimization; will audit mergeMetadata behavior. Propose hotfix: preserve per-tool idempotency headers during requeue and skip hash-based tool ordering when reconstructing partial batch. Also add end-to-end test covering transient stream resets.
Customer (Acme) (via CS): Impacted ~0.7% of runs in last 24h. Asks for immediate mitigation and whether we can replay/compensate duplicated side-effects.
resolution:
Workaround (temporary): disable batch coalescer for the customer's dedicated pool (config flag: coordinator.coalescer.enabled=false) and set coordinator.retry.reorder=false. This prevents metadata normalization and reordering.

Fix plan: engineering will land a two-step fix: (1) hotfix to preserve per-tool idempotency tokens in the requeue path (target patch 2026-03-13), (2) add e2e tests and change requeue reconstruction to preserve original tool order (target 2026-03-20).

Follow-ups:
- Run a targeted compensating job with the customer to deduplicate affected runs (Support + SRE + Customer).
- Postmortem entry and new test coverage.

Status: In Progress. Hotfix branch created: orchestrator/hotfix/preserve-tool-idempotency. Hotfix scheduled for canary 2026-03-13 08:00 UTC.
